description: Eight-bit shift register: each clock works out a new bit from the DATA, LOGIC and XOR jacks and pushes it in, with every bit on its own jack and four converters reading groups of them

params.text: Forces the bit going in to 1 on the next clock; in EDIT mode it pushes a 1 in straight away
Forces the bit going in to 0 on the next clock; in EDIT mode it pushes a 0 in straight away
Sets all eight bits to zero at once
Sets the voltage at which the DATA, LOGIC and XOR jacks count as high, 1V to 9V
Attenuates and inverts the THRES CV jack, -1 to 1, before that voltage is added to the THRES knob
Attenuates and inverts the four-bit converter reading bits 1 to 4, -1 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the four-bit converter reading bits 3 to 6, -1 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the four-bit converter reading bits 5 to 8, -1 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the eight-bit converter reading the whole register, -1 to 1
Hands the register over to the WRITE and ERASE buttons and stops the clock being read at all, so a pattern can be typed in by hand

inputs.text: The voltage read against the threshold to set the bit going in, unless a WRITE or ERASE button overrides it
A second voltage read against the threshold and combined with the DATA result by the logic operation the menu chooses; hovering the jack names the operation in use
A third voltage read against the threshold and exclusive-ORed with everything else to give the bit going in
Each rise past 1V works out the next bit and shifts the whole register along by one
A rise past 1V sets all eight bits to zero at once
Scaled by its attenuverter and added to the THRES knob, the total clamped to 1V and 9V

outputs.text: Bits 1 to 4 read as a four-bit number, 0V to 10V before its attenuverter
Bits 3 to 6 read as a four-bit number, 0V to 10V before its attenuverter
Bits 5 to 8 read as a four-bit number, 0V to 10V before its attenuverter
Its own bit of the register, put out as a gate, a copy of the clock or a short trigger depending on the menu
All eight bits read as one number, -5V to 5V before its attenuverter, or 0V to 10V with the menu set to unipolar

notes: with EDIT on the clock input is not read at all; the register only moves when WRITE or ERASE is pressed
a bit output patched back into DATA, LOGIC or XOR is handled specially: if that bit changed on the very clock being processed, its previous state is read, which keeps a feedback loop stable
that same handling means stacked cables into DATA, LOGIC or XOR are not read correctly; to merge sources, patch one into LOGIC and set the logic type to OR
a jack with no cable counts as low and takes no part in working out the next bit
every jack is monophonic, whatever is patched in
menu: Bit output mode: Clocks, Gates, Triggers — Clocks passes the CLOCK voltage through while the bit is high, Gates holds a flat 10V, Triggers sends a 1 millisecond pulse per clock
Logic type: XOR, NAND, XNOR, OR, AND, NOR — chooses how the LOGIC jack combines with the DATA result
Input overrides: Data, Everything — Data lets LOGIC and XOR act on a WRITE or ERASE press as well, Everything makes the button the whole answer
8 Bit DAC output: Bipolar, Unipolar — sets whether the eight-bit converter runs -5V to 5V or 0V to 10V
Show DAC lights — turns the converter lamps on and off
Show bit lights — turns the per-bit lamps on and off
